DIG-027.descricao_en: Generates personal data protection clauses ready for insertion in services, lease, employment, sale, agency (mandato) or other contracts, adapted to the type of contract and the data processing involved, in compliance with the GDPR and Law No. 58/2019.

DIG-028.titulo_en: Compliance Analysis of an AI System under the EU Artificial Intelligence Regulation
DIG-028.descricao_en: Generates a compliance analysis of an AI system under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), classifying the system's risk, identifying the obligations applicable to the provider and the user, and preparing recommendations for regulatory compliance.

DIG-029.descricao_en: Generates a complete cybersecurity Incident Response Plan (IRP), with procedures for detection, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons learned, aligned with the GDPR (notification to the CNPD within 72 hours), the NIS2 Directive (transposed by Law No. 65/2021) and ENISA/NIST good practice.

DIG-030.titulo_en: GDPR Compliance Checklist for Small Businesses
DIG-030.descricao_en: Generates a tailored GDPR compliance checklist for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), with an analysis of the current position and a prioritised action plan, adapted to the sector and the type of data processed, following the CNPD's guidance for SMEs.

DIG-031.titulo_en: Opinion on Processing Health Data / Special Categories
DIG-031.descricao_en: Generates an opinion on the lawfulness of processing health data or other special categories of personal data (Art. 9 GDPR), analysing the specific legal basis, the conditions for lawfulness, the enhanced security obligations and recommendations for compliance.

DIG-032.titulo_en: Digital Influencer Agreement and Advertising Disclosure
DIG-032.descricao_en: Generates a complete digital influencer agreement, covering the provision of commercial communication services on social media, advertising identification obligations (ICAP, Unfair Commercial Practices Directive), personal data protection (GDPR), intellectual property and image rights, adapted to the Portuguese market and EU law.

DIG-033.descricao_en: Determines whether a processing operation mandatorily requires a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA/AIPD) under Article 35 of the GDPR and the WP248 guidelines of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB/CEPD), taking into account the list of types of processing requiring a DPIA published by the CNPD under Article 35(4) of the GDPR.

DIG-034.titulo_en: Full DPIA for a Profiling and Automated Decision-Making System
DIG-034.descricao_en: Prepares a complete Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA/AIPD) for profiling and automated decision-making systems, following the methodology of Article 35 of the GDPR, the EDPB WP248 Guidelines and the CNIL PIA methodology, identifying and mitigating risks and recording the results for accountability purposes (Art. 5(2) GDPR).

DIG-035.titulo_en: Due Diligence on a Data Processor (GDPR Supplier)
DIG-035.descricao_en: Assesses the GDPR compliance of a data processor before the contract under Article 28 of the GDPR is concluded, analysing the technical and organisational guarantees required by Article 28(1), including certifications, security policies, server location, sub-processing arrangements and incident history.

DIG-036.titulo_en: Data Breach Notification to the CNPD — 72-Hour Deadline (Operational Guide)
DIG-036.descricao_en: Step-by-step operational guide for managing and notifying a personal data breach to the CNPD within the 72-hour deadline set by Article 33 of the GDPR, structuring the mandatory elements of the notification, the assessment of the risk to data subjects and the internal record of the incident under Law No. 58/2019 of 8 August (Portugal's GDPR implementing law).

DIG-037.titulo_en: International Data Transfers — Post-Schrems II Safeguards Analysis
DIG-037.descricao_en: Analyses the lawfulness of an international transfer of personal data to third countries in light of Articles 44 to 49 of the GDPR, taking into account the impact of the CJEU's Schrems II judgment (C-311/18), EDPB Guidelines 05/2021 on transfers, the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (2023 Adequacy Decision), the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by Commission Decision 2021/914, and the assessment of the level of protection in the destination country (Transfer Impact Assessment — TIA).

DIG-038.titulo_en: DPO Regime — Appointment, Duties and Management of Conflicts of Interest
DIG-038.descricao_en: Analyses whether a Data Protection Officer (DPO) must be appointed, the conditions for a valid appointment, the legal duties and the limits on holding the post, with particular focus on the prohibition of conflicts of interest in Article 38(6) of the GDPR, the EDPB WP243 guidelines on the DPO and Law No. 58/2019 (Articles 9 to 11).

DIG-039.titulo_en: AI Act Compliance — Risk Classification and Deployer Duties
DIG-039.descricao_en: Analyses the compliance of an artificial intelligence system with Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), determining the applicable risk category, the specific duties of the deployer (user of the AI system) under Articles 26 and 29 of the AI Act, and the additional obligations arising from its interplay with the GDPR, especially for high-risk systems that process personal data.

DIG-040.titulo_en: DSA Compliance — Duties of Marketplaces and Online Platforms
DIG-040.descricao_en: Analyses the compliance duties of a marketplace or online platform under Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act — DSA), identifying the category of platform (intermediary, hosting service, online platform, VLOP/VLOSE), the applicable obligations on transparency, content moderation, protection of minors and systemic risk management, and the interplay with the GDPR regarding users' personal data.

DIG-041.titulo_en: NIS2 — Assessment of Cybersecurity Duties for Essential and Important Entities
DIG-041.descricao_en: Assesses an organisation's cybersecurity and risk management obligations under Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2) and Decree-Law No. 65/2021 and its updated transposition, identifying the entity's category (essential or important), the mandatory risk management measures (Art. 21 NIS2), the obligations to report incidents to the competent authority (the National Cybersecurity Centre, CNCS, in Portugal), and the responsibilities of management bodies (Art. 20 NIS2).

DIG-042.titulo_en: Response to a Credential Stuffing Incident and Unauthorised Account Access
DIG-042.descricao_en: Legal and operational guide for responding to a credential stuffing attack (use of compromised third-party credentials for unauthorised access to accounts on the platform), covering the legal characterisation of the incident, the decision whether to notify the CNPD under Article 33 of the GDPR, communication to affected users, technical containment measures and parallel obligations under NIS2 and the Cybercrime Law (Law No. 109/2009).

DIG-043.titulo_en: Processing of Biometric Data — GDPR Compliance and Specific Requirements
DIG-043.descricao_en: Analyses the compliance of processing biometric data (fingerprints, facial recognition, voice, hand geometry) with Article 9 of the GDPR (special categories of data), the WP29 and EDPB guidance on biometric data, the specific requirements of Law No. 58/2019 (Article 28), and the implications of using biometric recognition systems under the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689).

DIG-044.titulo_en: Children's Data Online — Compliance with the GDPR, Law 58/2019 and the DSA
DIG-044.descricao_en: Analyses the specific requirements for protecting minors' personal data in information society services, including the consent regime of Article 8 of the GDPR and Article 16 of Law No. 58/2019 (minimum age of 13 in Portugal), age verification obligations, the prohibition of advertising targeted at minors under the DSA (Article 28 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065), and the UK Age Appropriate Design Code as a benchmark of good practice.

DIG-045.titulo_en: Pseudonymisation and Anonymisation — Legal and Technical Strategy
DIG-045.descricao_en: Analyses the legal distinction between pseudonymisation and anonymisation for GDPR purposes, assesses whether a data set is genuinely anonymous (and therefore outside the scope of the GDPR) in light of the criteria in WP29 Opinion 05/2014, and recommends pseudonymisation strategies compliant with Article 25 (privacy by design) and Article 89 (processing for archiving, research and statistical purposes) of the GDPR.

DIG-046.titulo_en: Privacy by Design — Implementation in Digital Systems and Products
DIG-046.descricao_en: Guide to implementing the principles of privacy by design and privacy by default under Article 25 of the GDPR, with practical application to software development, identification of dark patterns prohibited under EDPB Guidelines 03/2022, integration into the agile development cycle and documentation for accountability.

DIG-047.titulo_en: Health Data — Requirements for Processing, Sharing and the EHDS
DIG-047.descricao_en: Analyses the specific requirements for processing health data as a special category under Article 9 of the GDPR, Article 28 of Law No. 58/2019 and Law No. 12/2005 (genetic and health information), and the sharing rules in the context of the European Health Data Space (EHDS, Regulation (EU) 2025/327), with attention to digital health platforms and clinical research.

DIG-048.titulo_en: Processing of Criminal Data (Article 10 GDPR) — Conditions and Limits
DIG-048.descricao_en: Analyses the restrictive conditions for the lawful processing of data relating to criminal convictions and offences under Article 10 of the GDPR and Article 27 of Law No. 58/2019, focusing on corporate due diligence, background checks in recruitment, collaborative economy platforms and fit-and-proper requirements in the financial sector.

DIG-049.titulo_en: Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs) — Intra-Group Transfers and Approval
DIG-049.descricao_en: Analyses the Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs — Regras Vinculativas de Empresas) mechanism under Article 47 of the GDPR as a safeguard for international transfers within multinational groups, including the minimum content, the approval process by the CNPD (where it is the lead authority), the difference between controller BCRs and processor BCRs, and the use of SCCs during the approval period.

DIG-050.titulo_en: Artificial Intelligence Clauses in Contracts — GDPR and AI Act
DIG-050.descricao_en: Structures specific contractual clauses for contracts involving artificial intelligence systems, covering the allocation of responsibilities between the client (deployer) and the supplier (provider) under the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) and the GDPR, including clauses on audit, incident management, training data, explainability, human oversight and civil liability.

DIG-051.titulo_en: Workplace Video Surveillance — GDPR Compliance and Employment Law Limits
DIG-051.descricao_en: Analyses the compliance requirements for video surveillance systems in the workplace, including the legal basis under Article 6 and Article 9 of the GDPR (where biometric), the limits imposed by Article 20 of the Labour Code, the requirements of Law No. 34/2013 (private security) and Law No. 1/2005 (video surveillance on public roads), the DPIA obligation, and the prior licence or authorisation required.

DIG-052.titulo_en: Cross-Border Complaint to the Lead Authority — One-Stop-Shop Mechanism
DIG-052.descricao_en: Structures a data subject's complaint against a controller established in another EU Member State, using the one-stop-shop mechanism under Articles 56 and 77 of the GDPR, determining the competent data protection authority (lead supervisory authority) and describing the cooperation procedure between the CNPD and the lead authority under Article 60 of the GDPR.

DIG-053.titulo_en: Location Data and Device Tracking — ePrivacy and GDPR
DIG-053.descricao_en: Analyses the compliance requirements for processing device location data and tracking users (cookies, device fingerprinting, mobile SDKs) under Law No. 41/2004 (Portugal's transposition of the ePrivacy Directive), the GDPR, and EDPB guidance on cookies (Guidelines 05/2020) and location data (Guidelines 04/2021), focusing on the requirement of prior informed consent.

DIG-054.titulo_en: Exercise of the Right to Erasure Conflicting with a Legal Retention Obligation
DIG-054.descricao_en: Analyses and responds to requests to exercise the right to erasure (right to be forgotten) under Article 17 of the GDPR where it conflicts with legal data retention obligations (tax, accounting, employment, judicial), determining which data may be erased and which must be retained, and setting out the reasons in the reply to the data subject.

DIG-055.titulo_en: GDPR Compliance Programme for SMEs — Phased Implementation
DIG-055.descricao_en: Practical guide to the phased implementation of a GDPR compliance programme in a Portuguese small or medium-sized enterprise, with a prioritised action plan, the essential documentation to prepare and integration with an SME's typically limited resources, with reference to Article 5 (principles), Article 30 (record of processing activities — RAT), Article 32 (security) and Law No. 58/2019.

DIG-056.titulo_en: Joint Controller Agreement — Structure and Clauses (Article 26 GDPR)
DIG-056.descricao_en: Prepares a joint controller agreement for the processing of personal data under Article 26 of the GDPR, determining when two or more entities are joint controllers, the mandatory minimum content of the agreement, how it must be made available to data subjects, and joint and several liability towards data subjects and data protection authorities.

DIG-057.titulo_en: Notification of a High-Risk AI System to the National Competent Authority (AI Act)
DIG-057.descricao_en: Structures the notification and registration process for a high-risk artificial intelligence system under Articles 49 and 71 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), determining the national competent authority in Portugal, the documents to be submitted and the link with the EU Declaration of Conformity under Article 47 of the AI Act for Annex III high-risk systems.

DIG-058.titulo_en: GDPR Compliance Audit — Methodology and Report
DIG-058.descricao_en: Complete methodology for carrying out a GDPR compliance audit of an organisation, with an analysis framework by area, a compliance checklist, identification of non-conformities and the structure of the final report with prioritised recommendations, suitable for lawyers and data protection consultants.

DIG-059.titulo_en: B2B Direct Marketing — Legal Bases and Opt-Out (ePrivacy + GDPR)
DIG-059.descricao_en: Analyses the legal bases for sending electronic commercial communications in a B2B (business-to-business) context under Article 13 of Law No. 41/2004 (Portuguese ePrivacy law), the GDPR, and CNPD and EDPB guidance, distinguishing the B2B regime (where it is debated whether legitimate interest can be the basis) from the B2C regime (where prior consent is the rule), and structuring compliant opt-out mechanisms.

DIG-060.titulo_en: External Data Protection Officer — Services Agreement and Obligations
DIG-060.descricao_en: Structures the services agreement for an external Data Protection Officer (DPO), defining the legal obligations under Articles 37 to 39 of the GDPR and clauses on independence, confidentiality, availability and conflicts of interest, suitable for law firms, consultancies and independent professionals providing shared external DPO services to multiple clients in Portugal.
